h: Books, a pyramid and a queen with a local link
p: Blickling is a grand Jacobean house of red brick, with Dutch-style gables and a long approach flanked by yew hedges. That first view as you walk up is one of the best in Norfolk, so have your camera ready.

The estate is linked with Anne Boleyn, Henry VIII's second wife, as her family owned an earlier house here, and tradition has it she may have been born on the estate. The present house came later, but the story adds a romantic touch, and you will find a few nods to her as you explore.

Book lovers are spoilt here. The Long Gallery holds a huge historic library, with thousands of volumes lining the walls, and it is one of the most impressive rooms in any National Trust house. Take your time and look up at the elaborate plaster ceiling while you are there.

Out in the park, look out for the pyramid-shaped mausoleum, built for the 2nd Earl of Buckinghamshire, and the large lake, which makes a lovely backdrop for a picnic. There are plenty of waymarked walks across the estate.

Allow a full day. The pretty market town of Aylsham is just up the road, and from there the narrow-gauge Bure Valley Railway runs to Wroxham, the gateway to the Norfolk Broads, where you can hire a boat or take a river trip. Felbrigg Hall, another National Trust house, is also within easy reach, near Cromer on the coast.
